chapters.title: Meet Python
chapters.overview: Learn how Python represents information, displays results, and evaluates expressions.

concepts.name: Printing output
concepts.explanation: print() sends a value to the console so you can see what your program is doing.
concepts.practice: Print your name and the result of 12 multiplied by 4.
concepts.mistake: Forgetting quotation marks around text or placing the closing parenthesis incorrectly.

concepts.name: Strings
concepts.explanation: A string is text inside matching single or double quotation marks. Strings can contain spaces and punctuation.
concepts.practice: Create a message that combines a learner name with a welcome sentence.
concepts.mistake: Trying to add a string and a number without converting the number with str().

concepts.name: Integers and floats
concepts.explanation: Integers are whole numbers. Floats contain a decimal point. Python uses both for calculations.
concepts.practice: Calculate the cost of three notebooks priced at 2.50 each.
concepts.mistake: Expecting division with / to produce an integer; use // for floor division when appropriate.

concepts.name: Booleans and None
concepts.explanation: A boolean is True or False and is useful for decisions. None represents the absence of a value.
concepts.example:
is_ready = True
has_answer = False
selected_hint = None
concepts.practice: Create a boolean called has_completed and set it to False.
concepts.mistake: Writing true or false in lowercase; Python requires True and False.

concepts.name: Variables and assignment
concepts.explanation: A variable is a name pointing to a value. The equals sign assigns a value; it does not ask whether two values are equal.
concepts.practice: Create quest_xp with 50, then add 10 bonus XP.
concepts.mistake: Using a name before assigning it, using spaces in names, or confusing = with ==.

concepts.name: Operators and expressions
concepts.explanation: Arithmetic operators calculate values: +, -, *, /, //, %, and **. Comparisons produce booleans: ==, !=, >, <, >=, and <=.
concepts.practice: Check whether a learner with 240 XP has reached a 250 XP milestone.
concepts.mistake: Mixing operator precedence; use parentheses to make the intended order clear.

chapters.title: Make Decisions
chapters.overview: Teach programs to choose different actions using conditions.

concepts.name: Comparisons
concepts.explanation: Comparison operators produce True or False and let a program test a fact.
concepts.practice: Test whether a score is at least 70.
concepts.mistake: Using = instead of == in a comparison.

concepts.name: if and else
concepts.explanation: if runs a block when its condition is true; else runs when it is false.
concepts.practice: Display whether a learner passed a checkpoint.
concepts.mistake: Missing the colon or indentation after the condition.

concepts.name: elif and logical operators
concepts.explanation: elif handles another case. and, or, and not combine boolean conditions.
concepts.practice: Create three progress messages for beginner, growing, and advanced learners.
concepts.mistake: Putting broad conditions before more specific conditions.

chapters.title: Repeat Yourself
chapters.overview: Automate repeated work with loops and ranges.

concepts.name: for loops
concepts.explanation: A for loop visits each item in a sequence one at a time.
concepts.practice: Print each chapter title from a list.
concepts.mistake: Indenting the loop body incorrectly.

concepts.name: range
concepts.explanation: range creates a sequence of numbers and is useful when you know how many repetitions you need.
concepts.example:
for level in range(1, 4):
    print("Level", level)
concepts.practice: Print levels 1 through 5.
concepts.mistake: Forgetting that the stop value is excluded.

concepts.name: while loops
concepts.explanation: A while loop repeats while a condition remains true. Update its state so it can finish.
concepts.practice: Count down from five to one.
concepts.mistake: Creating an infinite loop by never changing the condition.

chapters.title: Lists
chapters.overview: Store and process ordered collections of values.

concepts.name: Creating and indexing
concepts.explanation: Lists use square brackets and zero-based indexes, so the first item is at position 0.
concepts.practice: Read the second item from a list of tools.
concepts.mistake: Using an index equal to the list length.

concepts.name: Changing lists
concepts.explanation: Lists are mutable: items can be replaced, appended, inserted, or removed.
concepts.practice: Add a new lesson and remove an old placeholder.
concepts.mistake: Expecting append to return the new list; it changes the list in place.

concepts.name: List loops
concepts.explanation: Loop through list items to process every value without repeating code.
concepts.practice: Print each score after adding a 10 point bonus.
concepts.mistake: Changing a list while iterating over it without care.

chapters.title: Functions
chapters.overview: Package reusable logic into named blocks that accept input and return results.

concepts.name: Defining and calling
concepts.explanation: def creates a function. Calling its name runs the indented body.
concepts.practice: Create a function that prints a quest title.
concepts.mistake: Defining a function without calling it.

concepts.name: Parameters
concepts.explanation: Parameters let a function work with different values supplied by the caller.
concepts.example:
def add_xp(current, bonus):
    return current + bonus
concepts.practice: Write a function that accepts a learner name and returns a greeting.
concepts.mistake: Passing arguments in the wrong order.

concepts.name: Return values
concepts.explanation: return sends a result back to the caller so it can be stored or used in another expression.
concepts.practice: Return True when a learner has enough XP to unlock a chapter.
concepts.mistake: Printing a result when the caller needs a returned value.

chapters.title: Strings
chapters.overview: Work confidently with text, formatting, and useful string methods.

concepts.name: Indexing and slicing
concepts.explanation: Strings are sequences, so you can select characters or ranges with indexes.
concepts.practice: Print the first three letters of a username.
concepts.mistake: Forgetting that the slice stop position is excluded.

concepts.name: Methods
concepts.explanation: Methods such as lower, upper, strip, replace, and split transform or inspect text.
concepts.practice: Normalize a name by removing spaces and making it lowercase.
concepts.mistake: Forgetting that most string methods return a new string.

concepts.name: f-strings
concepts.explanation: f-strings insert values into readable text using expressions inside braces.
concepts.practice: Build a progress message with a level and XP value.
concepts.mistake: Leaving out the f before the opening quote.

chapters.title: Dictionaries
chapters.overview: Represent structured information as key/value pairs.

concepts.name: Keys and values
concepts.explanation: A dictionary maps unique keys to values and uses braces with colon-separated pairs.
concepts.practice: Create a profile with a name, level, and XP.
concepts.mistake: Using a missing key without checking for it.

concepts.name: get and update
concepts.explanation: get safely reads optional keys, while assignment updates or adds a value.
concepts.practice: Add a streak field to a learner profile.
concepts.mistake: Assuming get changes the dictionary; it only reads it.

concepts.name: Looping dictionaries
concepts.explanation: items(), keys(), and values() let you process dictionary data.
concepts.example:
for skill, score in skills.items():
    print(skill, score)
concepts.practice: Print every skill and its score.
concepts.mistake: Modifying keys while looping through the dictionary.

chapters.title: Problem Solving
chapters.overview: Use a repeatable process to understand, test, and fix programs.

concepts.name: Read the error
concepts.explanation: Tracebacks identify the error type and the line where Python noticed the problem.
concepts.example:
# NameError means a name was used before it was defined
print(total)
concepts.practice: Read a traceback and identify the failing line.
concepts.mistake: Fixing the last line blindly instead of reading the error type.

concepts.name: Trace values
concepts.explanation: Print intermediate values to observe how data changes through a program.
concepts.example:
total = 0
for value in [2, 4, 6]:
    total += value
    print("total:", total)
concepts.practice: Trace a loop that calculates a total.
concepts.mistake: Changing multiple things at once and losing the cause of the bug.

concepts.name: Break into steps
concepts.explanation: Turn a large problem into small inputs, transformations, decisions, and outputs.
concepts.example:
# input -> process -> output
name = input("Name: ")
message = f"Hello, {name}"
print(message)
concepts.practice: Describe a quiz scorer as three small steps.
concepts.mistake: Starting to code before writing down the expected result.

chapters.title: Mini Project
chapters.overview: Combine variables, decisions, loops, and functions in a number guessing game.

concepts.name: Plan the game
concepts.explanation: Define the secret number, user input, attempts, and win condition before coding.
concepts.practice: Write the rules in plain language first.
concepts.mistake: Mixing input, game rules, and output into one untestable block.

concepts.name: Validate input
concepts.explanation: Convert input carefully and handle values outside the expected range.
concepts.practice: Reject guesses outside a chosen range.
concepts.mistake: Assuming every input can be converted to an integer.

concepts.name: Use a loop
concepts.explanation: Repeat guesses until the player wins or runs out of attempts.
concepts.example:
for attempt in range(3):
    print("Attempt", attempt + 1)
concepts.practice: Give the player three attempts and a final message.
concepts.mistake: Forgetting to stop after a correct guess.

chapters.title: Final Project
chapters.overview: Build a small text adventure that combines the core Python skills.

concepts.name: Design the story
concepts.explanation: Map locations, choices, consequences, and a clear ending before implementation.
concepts.practice: Draw three connected locations and two choices.
concepts.mistake: Creating choices that do not lead anywhere.

concepts.name: Model game state
concepts.explanation: Use dictionaries, lists, and variables to track inventory, health, and location.
concepts.practice: Add an item when the player searches a room.
concepts.mistake: Keeping the same state in several unrelated variables.

concepts.name: Combine the skills
concepts.explanation: Functions keep actions reusable, loops keep the game running, and decisions control outcomes.
concepts.practice: Create a playable path with one win and one lose ending.
concepts.mistake: Adding features before the smallest playable version works.
